Subject: Significant latency spikes and 429s affecting batch payments

Hi Karthik —

We're seeing repeated timeouts and 429s when we run our large batch payout job against the Redwood API during our nightly window (23:30 - 00:20 PT). Latency jumps from ~150ms to >2.5s and roughly 18% of requests get 429s; this is causing downstream retries and payment delays.

We haven't changed our traffic shape on our side — same job, same concurrency. Attached are sampling logs and a timeline from our side (slo-timeline.png). We need this prioritized: we have customers waiting and finance is calling.

Can you confirm whether this is on Redwood's side (rate limiting/quota/burst) or something in the path? If it's configuration, what is the rollback/mitigation ETA?

Thanks,
Amir Khan

Amir / team — initial triage from prod: we see correlated 429 spikes across the HelixPay tenant beginning 23:34 PT, coincident with a surge of long-sequence generation requests from a small subset of keys inside that batch run. Two findings so far: 

1) Burst-window misalignment: HelixPay's dedicated quota profile had an overlapping burst-credit window configured due to an infra consolidation change last week; the consolidation unintentionally mapped two quota buckets into the same burst pool. Requests hit the safety valve sooner than expected.

2) Request-braking behavior: when the burst pool was depleted, the runtime fell back to a stricter pacing regime (shorter refill window) which increased queueing latency and produced 429s while retries compounded the load.

Immediate ask: Amir, if you can temporarily stagger job shards (start times +/- 2m) it will reduce simultaneous pressure while we apply a short-term compensating increase to the HelixPay burst pool.

I'll attach the QoS sampling bundle (helix_agnostic-qos-logs.zip) after we scrub customer PII.

I'll follow with the targeted mitigation steps and a timeline.

—Laura
Sr. Product Manager, Redwood Console

Team / Amir — technical update and mitigation: 

Root cause (short): a quota mapping regression pushed HelixPay's high-priority bucket into a shared burst valve that had lower replenishment rates under sustained long-sequence workloads. The runtime's safety valve math then applied a more aggressive pacing profile (intended for low-priority tenants) when the shared pool crossed the threshold.

Evidence: sampling of token-throughput and KV-cache hit rates attached (see helix_agnostic-qos-logs.zip). We can reproduce the spike in staging by replaying the same request shape against the current kernel selection.

Immediate mitigations (30–90 min):
- Increase HelixPay dedicated burst credits by +40% (temporary) and raise refill rate for the specific high-priority bucket. Patch commands sent as patch-commands.txt (ops-safe list).
- Apply a hard cap on cross-tenant pool consumption to prevent bleed from other consolidated buckets.
- Enable emergency fallback to a compatible lighter-weight model variant for long-sequence requests to avoid KV cache pressure.

Operational note: this is a configuration-level regression introduced during an infra consolidation on 2026-12-02. No code-level rollback required, but we will push a policy cleanup to remove overlapping mappings.

Requesting approval to apply the +40% burst credits now. ETA for stabilization after change: ~18 minutes, monitoring window 60 minutes thereafter.

Jonas
Staff SRE, Runtime Operations
